description: Anonymous live-read latency after connection reuse, early cached responses and snapshot-before-notification publication.

environment.limitations: Local synthetic traffic; host-run API/worker/generator share CPU. No TLS, proxy, WAN, media or provider traffic. Each data container: 2 CPUs/1 GiB; PostgreSQL default 100 connections. Later phases have longer timelines and warmer caches.

configurations.final-shared: Default: four ASGI workers, no separate live pool.
configurations.final-bounded: Add --live-workers=2 (two WSGI workers, two blocking threads each).
configurations.final-four-workers: Add --live-workers=4 (four WSGI workers, two blocking threads each).

notes: Every final run fails the strict 100 ms live p95 gate. The fastest observed configuration is not a repeatability or production-capacity claim.
All four final runs completed 60 commands without missed write slots, HTTP/SSE errors or stale final views. All measured live reads were cache hits.

Fresh local synthetic stacks, 100 anonymous spectators, one match with 100 initial shots, writes every three seconds, reconnect halfway through. API, workers and generator share the host with other activity. No tests ran during the measured final phases.
A separate live pool changes process allocation. Production routing and service supervision are not changed by this patch; authenticated or filtered requests still use the complete API path.

Application timing excludes outer middleware, request scheduling and response completion. The per-request client-minus-application distribution includes those costs and transport; it is not a pure queue timer. Percentiles must not be subtracted from each other.
Historical baseline uses the previous publication artifact and its source hashes. These sequential measurements are not randomized or isolated hardware comparisons.

Exploratory 60-second results: shared clients 831.06 ms live p95; early cache dispatch 558.19 ms; separate ASGI pool 834.33 ms; separate WSGI pool with default thread count 197.51 ms. These pre-final source states are not acceptance results.
The cProfile diagnostic had five HTTP 500 responses and one missed write slot. Profiling timings were excluded from performance comparisons; subsequent unprofiled final runs had no HTTP errors.
